LONG_DESCRIPTION: Indonesia has the lowest rate of electrification of all the major economic powers in Asia, placing it behind other rising economies among the ASEAN states. As the use of renewable energy – in particular photovoltaics – is now a cost-optimized option in many off-grid settings, solar electricity will be used for many electrification projects. A central precondition for the successful implementation of these political targets is the use of safe, high-quality components and systems for renewable energy that are adapted to internat. standards. For this to be possible, the national QI has to render internationally recognized and demand-oriented services. The national quality infrastructure comprises metrology, standardization and testing, as well as conformity assessment, certification and accreditation. Currently, demand-oriented, recognized services are not provided in the national QI, or are not used effectively - as a result, the potential of photovoltaics is not sufficiently exploited.
